content.title: About
content.content: Lambsquarter (Chenopodium album), also known as goosefoot, is an annual herb widely distributed in temperate regions. When cooked, its leaves become tender with a mild nutty flavor and a hint of sweetness. Cooked lambsquarter is commonly used in soups, stews, and as a side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Lambsquarter has been consumed since ancient Greek and Roman times.
Its seeds are ground into a protein‑rich flour used for baking.
The plant grows quickly and is often called a "nutritional weed" because it can be harvested from the wild.
Leaves are high in vitamins A and C, as well as iron and calcium.
In some cultures the leaves are boiled with milk to make a nourishing drink.

items.title: Rich in vitamins A and C
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision and immunity, while vitamin C acts as an antioxidant protecting cells.

items.title: Source of iron and calcium
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Contains plant protein
items.content: Protein from lambsquarter helps meet daily amino‑acid needs, especially in vegetarian diets.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Cooked lambsquarter is virtually fat‑free, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber content promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: High oxalate levels may contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Some people may be allergic to plants in the amaranth family.

items.title: Raw toxicity
items.content: Raw leaves contain oxalic acid and should always be cooked before consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked lambsquarter can be served as a side dish, added to vegetable soups, stews, or salads. It is also used as a filling for pies and pancakes. Before cooking, rinse the leaves well and trim any tough stems.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked lambsquarter in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, freeze portions in freezer bags at –18 °C, where they retain quality for up to 2 months.
